items.title: A business worth building
items.body: The interesting part of a business is where the idea meets the real world: customers, operations, and something useful enough that people come back. My Now page records the current direction: starting a petfood business.
items.question: What would make someone come back?

items.title: Reading for better judgment
items.body: Books about business, psychology, philosophy, and lives well lived. The thread running through my reading notes is finding better questions and ideas that change the next decision.

items.title: The mind behind the decision
items.body: Bias, intuition, incentives, and the stories we tell ourselves. Thinking, Fast and Slow is one of the places this interest shows up on my bookshelf.
items.source: Notes on Thinking, Fast and Slow

items.title: A home for a curious mind
items.body: This website is an ongoing experiment in remembering more of life: books, thoughts, projects, people, and places, gathered somewhere I can return to and build on.

items.title: Culture is part of the product
items.body: How people work together can decide what a business becomes. My essay on “hot” and “warm” cultures explores the difference between a team that is comfortable and one that brings energy to the work.

items.title: Motorbikes, mountains, unfamiliar places
items.body: The Vietnam travel notes bring together a different kind of learning: new landscapes, street food, ancient temples, and time spent outside the familiar.

items.title: Attention is worth protecting
items.body: Technology can expand what we can do and quietly consume the time to do it. That tension sits at the heart of Feed My Addiction, alongside the focus on my bookshelf in Deep Work.
items.question: What are you feeding?

items.title: Small experiments, honest feedback
items.body: The Lean Startup and The Mom Test share a useful question: what evidence would show that an idea is worth pursuing? Customer conversations and small experiments make an interesting pair.

items.title: AI as a way to build
items.body: The appeal is practical: turning a question into a working tool, testing an idea, and shortening the distance between thinking about a project and making it. This site is a place to keep those experiments visible.

items.title: Writing to find the thought
items.body: Essays on attention, culture, endings, and beginnings. A place to work through an idea long enough to discover what is actually worth saying.

items.title: The lives behind the businesses
items.body: Founder stories make the decisions tangible: uncertainty, persistence, timing, and the work behind the eventual outcome. Shoe Dog is one of the biographies on my shelf.

items.title: Systems that make practice easier
items.body: Atomic Habits brings the focus back to everyday actions: the cue, the environment, the repetition. An interest in learning becomes more useful when it has somewhere to go each day.
